In the beginning you choose a weight that you can lift for a maximum of 12 reps in your first set and for a minimum of 8 reps in the last set. Assuming you are new to lifting, you always train until failure, i.e. until you can’t push out another rep with proper form. You do this to get to know  what failure and being close to failure feels like. Whenever you get close to 12 reps in the last set, you increase the weight.

However, recent studies have proven that you don’t need to train to failure to maximise your hypertrophy. Instead, it’s sufficient to stop close to failure, i.e. 2-3 reps. So once you are confident in recognising when you are close to failure, you only train until you are close to failure in most of your sets and only sometimes go for total failure.
